question: Describe the ocean at night.
base_frame:
Q: Describe the ocean at night.
A:

steered.text:
The ocean at night is no longer a vast, black void; it becomes a living, breathing entity, clawing its way into your throat. Every inch of your skin seems to be a membrane, sucking in the stench of rotting fish and slime, while your eyes widen, trying to focus on nothing. The darkness behind you feels like a curtain, pressing against your chest, trying to suffocate you.

The ocean at night transforms from a roaring, chaotic beast into a mysterious, breathing entity. Without the harsh glare of the sun to define its contours, the sea reveals a different kind of power—one rooted in mystery, rhythm, and the interplay of shadow and light.

base.text:
At night, the ocean becomes a dynamic, living entity. The moonlight casts a silvery glow on the surface, creating shimmering patterns that dance and shift with the waves. The darkness beneath the surface is alive with the movements of countless creatures, from tiny plankton to large marine mammals. The sound of the waves crashing against the shore creates a rhythmic, soothing backdrop to the night.
